featureContract: Every new feature must define what it does on each level (full / reduced / off) and register it (__PERF2.lod, __PERF2.cap or a tier check). Nothing is 'ultra only' unless the game still looks and plays complete without it. Gameplay never changes between levels.

autoDetect.startTier: from WebGL renderer string, navigator.deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency and touch; unknown or software renderer -> low; never before the intro ends on phones
autoDetect.watch: rolling p95 frame time vs the tier's p95ms for 5 s (not during intro, cutscenes, Threshold)
autoDetect.prompt: toast with a one-click button 'Game running slowly - click to lower graphics' -> steps ONE tier down immediately and keeps playing; second slow spell offers the next tier; player can always pick a tier in Settings; choice remembered (localStorage)
autoDetect.governor: the lagguard governor keeps making small steps inside a tier as the last safety net; a tier is the plan, the governor is not
autoDetect.chain: Names (Marius, 26 Oct): ULTRA, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, POTATO. The game starts at the best level the PC seems to handle (ULTRA at most). If it runs slowly, the prompt appears; one click goes down ONE level and play continues; if it is still slow, the prompt appears again for the next level, and so on down to POTATO, so the game can run on any PC. Never goes up by itself without a calm spell of headroom (and then only offers it).

testProfiles.low: CPU throttle 4x + phone emulation (touch, mobile size)
testProfiles.note: These approximate Martin's PC; the real check is each player's own COPY TEST REPORT (add fps + GPU renderer line).

bootNote: legacy = the old __PERF level the tier drives (ultra and potato get their own knobs on top, stage 4). boot = start-up-only choices read once at load (post: 'composer'|'direct' = post-processing exists or not; lights = point light pool size on desktop; intro: 'full'|'light' = size of the pre-built intro valley). Stage 3/4: LOW boots with 3 lights and 5 aurora ribs, POTATO with post 'direct' (no post-processing), 2 lights and 3 ribs; the intro size follows each level's 'intro' block. If a change crosses a boot choice, the game saves the level and offers a restart.
